clesRetenues: Q Michael Ryskin (BofA) - how to achieve the H2 acceleration given the weak Q1 core (0,5%): three tailwinds expected (easing of the China Diagnostics headwinds, easier respiratory comps, improvement in Life Sciences consumables), all confirmed in Q1 according to management.

Q Vijay Kumar (Evercore) - strategic rationale for the Masimo acquisition and expected returns: mission-critical player in acute care, pull-through synergies with Radiometer, 125 M$ of cost synergies targeted by year 5, high-single-digit ROIC targets.
Q Vijay Kumar - why the Q2 margin decline is sharper than the historical pattern: seasonal respiratory decline, plus growth investments pulled forward from later quarters into Q2.
Q Scott Davis (Melius) - oil/petrochemical cost pressures, Middle East exposure: no significant cost pressure at this stage, no direct Middle East exposure in the supply chain.
Q Jack Meehan (Nephron) - influence of AI on customer spending: accelerates pharmaceutical development, improves pipeline yields (~10% base), stimulates demand for automation/instruments/reagents.
Q Jack Meehan - internal AI productivity benefits at Danaher: 'AI-enabled DBS' and 'DBS-enabled AI' increasingly synonymous, efficiency gains and accelerated product development cycles.

Q Tycho Peterson (Jefferies) - bioprocessing order trends by customer segment, size of the China opportunity: robust pharma demand in commercial production, biotech stabilising, CDMO improving, China biologics growing double digits.

Q Tycho Peterson - Life Sciences positioning for the remainder of the year: consumables now expected positive for the full year 2026 (vs a slight decline expected previously), China instruments in reinvestment, academic remains subdued but stable.

Q Casey Woodring (JPMorgan) - sequential context of bioprocessing orders and book-to-bill: Q1 = first positive order growth in nearly two years, robust funnel, larger order sizes (brownfield/greenfield).

Q Casey Woodring - what offsets the weaker respiratory guidance while keeping the diagnostics guidance unchanged: share gains at Cepheid, strong non-respiratory performance ex-China, DxI 9000 traction at Beckman Coulter, Masimo will bring an additional uplift.

Q Dan Brennan (TD Cowen) - M&A prioritisation by segment, another sizable deal possible this year: disciplined three-vector M&A filter, bias for capital deployment towards M&A, balance sheet and leadership capacity for several concurrent transactions.

Q Doug Schenkel (Wolfe) - what would allow the high end of the annual guidance to be reached: further Life Sciences improvement, acceleration in bioprocessing consumables/equipment, an above-normal respiratory season (return to the 1,8 Md$ endemic run rate).
Q Doug Schenkel - can Danaher pursue M&A in Diagnostics alongside the Masimo integration: yes, balance sheet and leadership capacity to execute across the three segments simultaneously.

Q Michael Ryskin (BofA) - why the Q2 bioprocessing shortfall (~75 M$) would not come back in Q3/Q4: ~50-60 M$ of chromatography resin shipments pushed to 2027 for reasons of customer planning/site readiness, ~100 M$+ on a full-year basis, but consumables/equipment order growth still robust at mid-single-digit %.

Q Tycho Peterson (Jefferies) - bioprocessing equipment outlook after 4 consecutive quarters of order growth: 'early innings' of a multi-year capacity expansion cycle (reshoring), greenfield investments requiring 2-3 years to materialise.

Q Tycho Peterson - drivers of the conversion of biotech funding into consumables spending: improved biotech funding translating into orders/revenue, IDT progress in MRD testing, Aldevron momentum, Abcam's best quarter since the acquisition.

Q Dan Leonard (RBC) - what the customers delaying chromatography shipments have in common: delays confined to resin products for large-batch manufacturing at a few large commercial manufacturers, with no link to specific molecules or geographies.

Q Dan Leonard - driver of the Q4 diagnostics acceleration (high-single-digit) given the flat Q3 guidance: excluding the respiratory headwind, diagnostics showed mid-single-digit core growth in Q2, product innovations (DxI 9000, Cepheid menu extensions) supporting the acceleration.

Q Scott Davis (Melius) - first Masimo metrics (closed early June): high-single-digit revenue growth in the quarter, FDA 510(k) clearance already obtained for an AI solution detecting opioid-induced respiratory depression.
Q Scott Davis - timing of the academic/government recovery: depends on more constructive government policies, academic <5% of revenue, stability rather than recovery is the current expectation.

Q Jack Meehan (Operon) - breakdown of semiconductor vs other customer growth at Pall: microelectronics (semiconductors/memory) grew above the segment rate (>10%), supported by a new Singapore site and capacity investments.
Q Jack Meehan - why Life Sciences slows from 5,5% in Q2 to an implied 3-4% in Q3: no change in the underlying trend, moderation tied to timing at Pall and project calendar variations.

Q Vijay Kumar (Evercore) - first FY2027 perspectives given the implied Q4 at ~6% and the 100 M$ bioprocessing pushout: the mid-single-digit core guidance for 2026 (not 2027) remains anchored at the low end of the 3-4% range, better Life Sciences offsetting more conservative bioprocessing assumptions.
Q Vijay Kumar - components of the 0,10$ EPS guidance raise: ~0,07-0,08$ tied to the early closing of Masimo (originally modelled for 2027), ~0,07-0,08$ of Q2 operating beat, partly offset by mix/FX.

Q Dan Brennan (TD Cowen) - does the mid-single-digit bioprocessing guidance include a cushion given the 100 M$+ pushout: impact of a few hundred basis points on bioprocessing growth, mid-single-digit progression expected in Q3 and mid-to-high-single-digit in Q4.

Q Dan Brennan - details on what the bioprocessing customers have in common, risk of recourse: delays limited to a few large customers, with no molecule/geography link, confidence that the 2027 shipments will indeed take place.

Q Casey Woodring (JPMorgan) - does the timing of consumables orders include the deferred revenue: delayed shipments already in the order book (not book-and-turn), most consumables shipped from the backlog.
Q Casey Woodring - updated Radiometer/Leica Biosystems outlook for H2: both continue at high-single-digit, the StatLab acquisition strengthens Leica's complete workflow offering.

Q Patrick Donnelly (Citi) - why several customers delayed simultaneously, delays extending beyond resins: the delays involve 'a few' very large customers (not several), limited to specialised resins, strong upstream consumables growth elsewhere in the portfolio.

Q Patrick Donnelly - what signals point to a turn in market confidence: segment growth of 5,5% driven by the pharma/biopharma recovery, improved biotech funding conversion, academic stabilisation, solid clinical/applied markets, Abcam's best quarter, emerging demand for AI automation.

Capital deployment flywheel active: Masimo closed early June ('every bit the company we thought', high-single-digit growth validated, FDA 510(k) already secured for an AI opioid-induced respiratory depression solution); Leica Biosystems to acquire StatLab (~$250M revenue, >85% recurring, accretive in year one, closing by end-2026); ~$900M of buybacks (5M shares); Diagnostics ex-respiratory +5% with Cepheid non-respiratory +low-double-digits and China stabilizing.

hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Quality serial-acquirer compounder (DBS) in cyclical bioprocessing reacceleration, now extended into patient monitoring/acute care via Masimo (closed EARLY, 10/06/2026, 9.9bn cash). Q2 26 reads double: at headline, a clean beat plus an annual adjusted-EPS raise (8.45-8.60); in the detail, core revenue growth NARROWED (top cut from +6% to +4%) on bioprocessing deliveries pushed into 2027 - the EPS raises are cost/mix-driven, not volume-driven.

== THESIS READ ==
- Bioprocessing timing slip, not demand loss: deliveries move to 2027, backing the 2027 acceleration in the model. Watch: bioprocessing orders/book-to-bill each quarter.
- Masimo integration is the new-money swing: closed early, funded in cash, net debt jumps to ~22bn in 2026 then deleverages ~4.5bn/yr. Watch: Masimo margin trajectory under DBS.
- The 2027+ financial-charge extrapolation (~-470M annualized from H2-26 run-rate, NOT the Treasury formula) is flagged LOW CONFIDENCE. Watch: reconfirm at the 10-Q - the single most uncertain bridge line.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Base = normalized US GAAP: acquisition amortization KEPT (reintegrated from the non-GAAP guide), true one-offs excluded (2025 impairment; Masimo transaction costs/inventory step-up ~0.15/share in Q2). Omnium EPS = non-GAAP guide minus after-tax amortization - the definitional wedge vs the 8.44 street is documented in the scorecard. 2026 financial charge explicitly guided (-310M).

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
2026: revenue 26.4bn (incl. Masimo stub), EBIT 5.67bn, ETR 17% (guided); 2027-2030: core +5%/yr with 2027 bioprocessing catch-up, margin drift, deleveraging 22 -> 4bn. Shares ~707M near-frozen 2026, gradual buyback resumption 2027+. Watch: financial-charge line vs 10-Q; Masimo synergy quantification; China diagnostics pricing.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 (Oct); bioprocessing order inflection; first full Masimo quarter; 2027 guidance (Jan) with the delivery catch-up.

ancrages.moteur: FY26 core revenue growth narrowed by management to +3,0/+4,0% (vs +3,0/+6,0% previously); translated into +3,5% central + FX +0,5%.
Masimo closed on 10/06/2026 (ahead of schedule), consolidated for ~6,5 months in 2026 (~840M$ of estimated incremental revenue on an annualised base of ~1,55 Md$), full year from 2027.
Gradual reacceleration of the core (multi-year bioprocessing + diagnostics ex-respiratory guided to accelerate) towards ~4,5-5%/yr over 2027-2030; FX neutralised beyond 2026.
Acquisition intangibles amortisation guided for FY26 at ~1,9 Md$ (vs 1,7 Md$ ex-Masimo); recurring charge reincorporated into the Omnium base (serial acquirer rule), rising in full-year 2027.
FY26 net financial charge explicitly guided by management at ~-310 M$ (E5-a bis priority, rate communicated).

Absent explicit guidance beyond 2026, extrapolation of the implied H2-26 run rate (~-460/470 M$ annualised, derived from H1-26 net interest vs the FY26 guide) rather than the Treasury 10Y+2pts formula (~6,55%) which would greatly overstate the actual observed cost (mix of existing low-coupon debt + partly short-term Masimo financing); then a decline as leverage comes down.
ETR normatif maintenu a 17% (guidance management inchangee).
Buybacks paused to fund Masimo (average shares guided at ~707M for FY26); gradual resumption assumed over 2027-2030 as leverage comes down.
Masimo transaction costs/inventory step-up (0,15$/share in Q2, ~108M$ pretax) treated as a genuine one-off tied to an identified transaction and excluded from the normalised base.

Isolated Life Sciences brand impairment in Q2 25 (432M$ pretax/328M$ after tax) + Biotechnology facility in Q1 25 (15M$/11M$): genuine one-offs not adjusted out at initial creation, corrected here via d-bis. Residual non-EBIT portion of the FY25 GAAP/non-GAAP bridge (~273M$ after tax in H2) treated as non-EBIT by approximation, not individually traced.
